title: Psalm 121: Morning Prayer For Protection and Safety
text: [Music] There are moments in life when we feel exposed, vulnerable to worry, exhaustion, or the unknown ahead. In those moments, our natural instinct is to look for help, for something or someone to hold on to. Psalm 121 is a timeless reminder that our true help does not come from what surrounds us, but from the one who made us. It is a quiet anchor for restless souls, a song for those walking through shadowed places. This prayer is an offering that responds to the psalm line by line, not as a formal exposition, but as a personal cry to the God who watches over us, both in the silence of night and in the demands of day. May these words become your own as you lift your eyes to the Lord. I lift up my eyes to the hills. From where does my help come? My help comes from the Lord who made heaven and earth. He will not let your foot be moved. He who keeps you will not slumber. Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep. The Lord is your keeper. The Lord is your shade on your right hand. The sun shall not strike you by day, nor the moon by night. The Lord will keep you from all evil. He will keep your life. The Lord will keep your going out and your coming in from this time forth and forever more. Lord, I lift my eyes to you. I lift them because I've run out of places to look. The hills ahead of me are too steep. the road too long and the burden too great. And still, even in my weakness, I choose to lift my eyes. Not because I am strong, but because I know where my help comes from. It doesn't come from the path behind me, or the journey ahead. It doesn't come from my effort, my will, or my plans. It comes from you. You who made heaven and earth. You who made me. You who breathed stars into the sky and shaped mountains with a whisper. You are not too distant to care. You are not too holy to draw near. My help comes from you. Not occasionally, not hopefully, but surely, constantly. You will not let my foot be moved. Even when I'm unsure, even when I walk with trembling steps, you steady me. You uphold me. When the ground beneath me feels uncertain, you remain unshaken. You keep me from falling. When I cannot balance myself, when I want to give up, you hold me firm. And you do this not just now and then, but always. Because you do not sleep. You do not slumber. You don't miss anything. You don't take breaks or turn away or blink. You don't forget where I am or what I need. You don't tire of watching over me. You are constant, more than the rising sun, more than the ticking clock, more than anything else in my life. You never slumber, Lord. You never stop keeping me. You who keep Israel, you keep me, too. You are the same God who led Abraham through lands unknown, who stayed with Joseph through betrayal and prison, who protected Ruth in her poverty, who walked with David through caves and coronations. You kept them, and you keep me. I am not overlooked. I am not forgotten. I am not too small for your care. I am kept. Not by chance, not by circumstance, but by you. You are my keeper. Not just my helper or rescuer, but the one who stays. You are my keeper, the one who remains when others walk away. You are my protector, my defender, my steady place in a spinning world. You are my shade at my right hand. Close, present, real. You cover me when life scorches. You protect me from the harshness of this world. When pressures feel like heat, when fear feels like glare, when expectations are too much to bear, you are the cool shelter I didn't know I needed, you stand right beside me, not above me in accusation, but beside me in love. The sun will not strike me by day, nor the moon by night. You know what drains me in the brightness, and what haunts me in the dark. You know the loud places of my life and the quiet ones, the relentless demands and the subtle anxieties. The moments when I am overwhelmed and the ones where I feel nothing at all. You are there in all of it. In every hour, every shift from light to dark, from joy to sorrow, from clarity to confusion. You are constant. You shelter me when I don't even know I need it. You protect me when I cannot see the danger coming. You preserve me when I can't hold myself together. You keep me from all evil, from harm that wounds the soul, from voices that try to destroy, from fear that tries to paralyze. You protect me from bitterness, from hopelessness, from the temptation to give up. You shield my heart from the arrows of accusation. You guard my thoughts when they wander into doubt. You keep me fully, tenderly, patiently. You keep my life. Not just my outer circumstances. Not just the days I wake up and go to sleep. You keep my actual life. My soul, my center, my identity. When I feel like I'm falling apart, you hold what matters most. When everything feels uncertain, you protect what's eternal. When I don't know who I am anymore, you remind me I am yours. You keep me not to control me, but to preserve me. You keep me so that nothing, no pain, no past, no mistake, no loss can take away what you have given. You keep my going out and my coming in. Every step I take, every errand, every meeting, every goodbye, every return. You are there when I leave, and you are there when I come back. You are there in the mundane and in the sacred. You are there when I travel to far places and when I sit in the stillness of home. You are not far. You are in the rhythm of my days. You are not just with me on Sundays or in moments of crisis, but in every hallway I walk, in every conversation I have, in every breath I take. You keep me from beginning to end. And not just today, not just this season, not just when I'm young or strong or full of hope. You keep me from this time forth and forever more. There is no end to your presence, no edge to your mercy, no limit to your protection. You keep me through the years, through the seasons, through the changes, through the aging, through the weeping and the rejoicing, through death, and even into life everlasting. You will keep me when I am old and frail. You will keep me when I take my last breath. And even then, you will not let me go. So I lift my eyes again, not just to the hills, but beyond them, to you, Lord, my maker, my keeper, my shade, my watchman, my strength, my help, my God. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you always.
